title: COP31 first draft calls for faster fossil-fuel phase-out; India says no new obligations
dek: The draft also asks rich countries to reach net zero by 2030 and to triple adaptation finance to at least 20 billion. India's environment minister told the summit developing countries must chart their own paths.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The first draft of the main political decision at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, calls for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels", asks developed countries to aim for net zero emissions by 2030, and says finance for adaptation should be tripled to at least $120 billion. The 18-page text, published on Monday by the summit's presidency, is an opening offer: it has to be agreed by consensus among nearly 200 countries before the summit ends on Friday, and several of its options are likely to be cut.

India set out its own red lines the same day. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav told a ministerial meeting on a "just transition" that developing countries "must be free to chart their own pathways without facing additional obligations", according to reports.

## What the draft says

The "cover decision", dated 16 November at 12:40, covers the summit's main themes. Among its provisions:

- Fossil fuels: paragraph 65 reaffirms the 2023 Dubai agreement on "transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner", and paragraph 66 goes further, calling for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels, including through the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems". The word "phase out" has been fought over at every summit since 2021.
- Rich countries: paragraph 25 "recognizes that developed countries should take the lead, including the call to achieve net zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2040", two decades earlier than most of their current targets.
- Adaptation: paragraph 73 says tripling adaptation finance "should reach at least USD$120 billion", and asks for a time-bound pathway to triple it by 2035 within the goal agreed in 2024 of at least $300 billion a year in climate finance by 2035.
- Electricity: it calls on countries to help raise electricity's share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, a priority of the Turkish hosts.
- Warming: it expresses "deep concern" that peak warming is projected to exceed 1.5°C and resolves to bring it back below 1.5°C "as early as possible within this century".
- Pledges: it commends the 163 countries that had submitted new national climate plans by 9 November.

Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who chairs the negotiations under an arrangement in which Türkiye hosts the summit, said the draft was not final. "There are elements in this draft that not all parties will agree on. That is a given," he said, according to reports. "What we'll be concentrating on in coming days are those issues where people can find common ground." Both the "phase out" and the "transitioning away" options could be dropped from the final text, according to reports.

## India's position

Mr Yadav, speaking at the fourth high-level ministerial roundtable on just transition, said there could be no "one-size-fits-all" model and that developing countries needed finance, technology transfer and help building capacity, according to reports. He said a proposed Just Transition Mechanism should "neither prescribe uniform sectoral pathways nor create new obligations", and backed a two-tier mechanism guided by countries, with the existing UAE Just Transition Work Programme kept as a forum for dialogue.

India has consistently resisted any phase-out of fossil fuels that singles out coal, its main source of electricity, and insists on the Paris Agreement principle, which the draft repeats, of "common but differentiated responsibilities", meaning richer countries that caused most past emissions should cut faster and pay more. The adaptation money matters directly to India, where heatwaves, cyclones and floods are growing more frequent: Cyclone Akvan is forecast to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on Friday, the summit's last scheduled day.

## What happens next

Negotiators will work through the draft this week, with new versions expected before ministers try to close a deal by Friday, 20 November. Climate summits frequently run beyond their scheduled end.
